column1: # <logical-addr> \t <comment>   appended after the '-' in the annotated listing.
# Blank lines and #-comments are ignored. Grows as routines are traced.

column2: arm page 0 (PB=0) for the branch below
S=1 so this is taken: jump to 00:00, the real boot init
copy within file0:  word0 -> word4,  word1 -> word5
broadcast file0 words 4,5 into files 2 and 3
CALL 0f:37 handles word 4; then TCY 5 + fall-through handles word 5
Y = 15; begin clearing R outputs from the top
loop: clears R15..R0 (all output/strobe lines off)
return; at boot the call stack is empty, so execution falls through to 00:05
X = 0: clear file 0 inline (the reusable subroutine entry is 00:06)
loop: zero all 16 words of file X
return; at boot falls through to the file-1..7 clears below
clear file 7  -- all 128 RAM nibbles are now zero
CALL 0e:02 (drives a nibble onto output lines R7..R10)
enter the interpreter main loop at 7:1d
... latch the K return lines into A
OR handler (opcode A): Rd <- Rd OR Rs
load Rd = R[M(1,0)] into scratch M(4,15)   [calls 16:1b]
store Rs into scratch M(4,14)  (now M(4,15)=Rd, M(4,14)=Rs)
bitwise OR: for each set bit of Rd (M(4,15)), set that bit in M(4,14) ...
... then write the OR result (M(4,14)) back to Rd via 15:2f
RUN CHECK: is the execute-this-pass flag M(0,8) bit 3 set?
clear -> hand off to the idle / keypad handler at 1e:1a
clear the flag for this pass ...
fetch DEST register: Y=0 -> uses M(1,0); returns R[M(1,0)] in A and scratch M(4,15)  (via 17:02)
fetch SOURCE register: Y=M(1,1); returns R[M(1,1)] in A; leaves X=4 for the caller
EXECUTE ONE INSTRUCTION. First advance the PC (2 nibbles: file 2, words 5:4)
A = PC-low + 1  (S set if PC-low was 15 -> carry into PC-high)
on carry, propagate into PC-high at 08:08
PC-low wrapped: store 0 and step Y to the high nibble
copy the new PC to the SRAM address pointer + a file-3 backup ...
now fetch the instruction's nibbles from external SRAM at that address ...
-> SRAM read routine at 9:02 (loads M(1,2)=opcode, M(1,1)/M(1,0)=operands; see the SRAM pass)
post-fetch: branch on state/opcode-class flags, then dispatch (opcode-dispatch pass)

column1: # ===== Page 17: operand resolution + register write-back (chapter 1, page 7) =====

column2: resolve SOURCE operand: Y=M(1,1); fetch R[M(1,1)] into A and scratch M(4,15)
shared entry: caller pre-loads Y with which operand nibble to use (Y=0 -> dest reg M(1,0))
stash the resolved value in ALU scratch M(4,15)
WRITE-BACK: store A into the destination register R[M(1,0)]
also keep a copy in temp M(1,15)
take the IMMEDIATE operand: A = M(1,1) (the literal middle digit), into scratch M(4,15)
MOV: R[dest] = A     -> write-back at 17:10.  Net: Rd <- Rs
MOVI: R[dest] = A    -> write-back at 17:10.  Net: Rd <- n

column1: # ===== Page 11: secondary dispatch (0..4) and F-group (by 2nd digit) =====

column2: F-GROUP dispatch on the second digit M(1,1)
2nd digit 0..8 -> 12:00 (F0x ext ops, DISP F1..F6, MAS F7, INV F8)
ADD/ADDI tail: A=Rd, add the resolved operand, set CARRY, write back to Rd
AMAAC: A = Rd + M(4,15) = Rd + operand; S = carry (sum > 15)
no carry -> clear CARRY = M(4,13) bit 0
write the sum back to Rd (-> write-back at 17:10)

column1: # ----- Page 16: SUB/SUBI + CMP/CMPI (subtract, set carry=no-borrow & zero) -----

column2: CMPI handler (opcode 9): compute Rd - n, set flags, discard the difference
CMP handler (opcode 8): compute Rd - Rs, set flags, discard the difference
SAMAN: A = M(4,15) - A = Rd - operand; S set if NO borrow (Rd >= operand)
no borrow -> set CARRY = M(4,13) bit 0  (carry is "no borrow" on subtract)
CPAIZ: negate the difference; S set if the difference was zero
SUBI handler (opcode 7): load Rd and immediate n; difference computed + stored to Rd
SUB handler (opcode 6): load Rd (source via 16:20); difference stored back to Rd

column1: # ----- Page 14: control flow (GOTO / CALL / BRC / BRZ) -----

column2: GOTO handler (opcode C): PC <- target address (M(1,1):M(1,0)) minus 1
copy the 2-digit target operand into the SRAM pointer M(1,5):M(1,4)  (via 0f:2b)
DMAN: target-low - 1 (pre-decrement; the fetch's pre-increment then lands on the target)
store the new PC into file 2 (PC) and file 3 (backup): low nibble ...
BRC handler (opcode D): branch iff CARRY (M(4,13) bit 0) is set
carry set -> take the branch by reusing the GOTO handler (14:00)
carry clear -> skip: go fetch the next instruction (08:02)
BRZ handler (opcode E): branch iff ZERO (M(4,13) bit 1) is set
CALL handler (opcode B): save the return address, then jump like GOTO
XMA: exchange PC-low with the target (old PC-low into A)
save old PC-low as the return address in M(1,13)
XMA: exchange PC-high with the target
save old PC-high as the return address in M(1,14)
now set the PC to the target (-> 14:05), like GOTO
helper: A <- R[M(1,0)] = the destination register Rd (also stashed in M(1,15))
SHR body (F9d): shift Rd right one bit (bit tests/sets on the register nibble)
SHL body (FAd): load Rd, then shift it left one bit
ANDI handler (opcode 3): load Rd and immediate n, then bitwise-AND
AND handler (opcode 2): load Rd and Rs, then bitwise-AND
bitwise AND: clear each result bit where the other operand's bit is 0
register write-back tail: store the ALU result (M(4,14)) into Rd, then continue
READ INSTRUCTION from SRAM into M(1,2):M(1,1):M(1,0)
set R11 = the KL selector -> routes the SRAM L data lines onto the K bus
put the instruction's SRAM address on the output lines (via 0b:20)
settle delay for the SRAM access (0e:36)
A = K = the L data nibble
invert it (SRAM data is stored complemented) via 09:23
set R5 -> select the middle nibble
... set R4 -> select the last nibble
clear R11 -> KL back to keyboard-scan mode
helper: one's-complement the nibble in A (flip all 4 bits)
SRAM settle delay: count A 0->15 twice, then return (waits for valid data)
set up the SRAM address: drive M(1,5):M(1,4) onto the address lines
TDO: present the address nibble on the O output lines
address-output helper: clock the nibble's bits out on R6
place the 4 bits of a nibble onto output lines R0..R3
